rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 3-4 and Table 4 report the authors' own prototype (NodeMCU/Arduino sensors, ThingSpeak cloud), a 3,000-record dataset of soil moisture, temperature, humidity and pump status, and their own ML classification results (accuracies 98.3-99.8%).
rows.notes: The study is a primary study, but it concerns an IoT sensor-based automated sprinkler irrigation prototype that predicts pump on/off from soil moisture, temperature and humidity using KNN, NB, RF, SVM and LR. It contains no remote sensing, no disease detection, no weed or pest control, and no robots; crop health monitoring and disease/weed control are only mentioned in passing in the literature review (ref. 28). No own result on the technology (remote sensing/AgroBots) or the effect (pest/disease/weed control) in the passage. Technology mismatch: in-situ IoT sensors and ML for irrigation scheduling, not remote sensing for pest control.

notes: Full text appears complete. Study is an IoT/ML irrigation-scheduling prototype in Rajasthan; it has no bearing on remote sensing, disease detection or weed/pest control. Reported accuracies are model classification metrics for pump state, not an agronomic effect.
